$comment: Explicit term lists for the cross-language harness parity fixture. Both needles and scripts/perf/harness-parity.mjs read this file; expected.json in the same directory is machine-generated from it and must never be hand-edited. mode=explicit: both sides bypass their own tokenizer (TS gets a weight-1 term map, Python gets _search_score with the same list) so the scores are comparable. mode=tokenized: both sides run their own production tokenizer over python_query, which is where the documented divergences live.

cases.name: parity
cases.python_query: worktree session quantum harness ledger digest 登录 修复 rlm embedded
cases.note: One kind as the corpus, explicit terms, every weight 1, every field a string, distinct positive scores above the cut: the digest window and harness.search must return the same ids in the same order.

cases.name: tie_window
cases.note: The tie group lands inside the visible window, so the two documented tie-breaks (TS identifier order, Python updated_at desc) pick different rows.

cases.name: tokenizer_floor
cases.python_query: rlm api мир 世界 worktree
cases.note: Python keeps three-character ASCII and two-character non-ASCII runs; the TS digest tokenizer cuts everything non-CJK below four characters.

cases.name: nonstring_path
cases.note: mem_numeric_path persists path as a number: the Python loader coerces it to 'general', the TS loader leaves it non-string and the identifier slot loses it.

cases.name: df_corpus
cases.python_query: worktree session quantum harness ledger digest 登录 修复 rlm embedded
cases.note: Python search(kind=None) merges every kind into one document-frequency corpus; the TS digest always ranks one kind at a time.

cases.name: weights
cases.note: The production digest weights goal terms 3 and recent-message terms 2 -> 1.5 -> 1 (agent-session.ts _buildHarnessDigestQueryTerms); harness.search has no weight face.
